_readme: Edit this file to update the app. Everything here is visible to players. Keep secrets in your notes app. IDs must be lowercase, no spaces. Ties only need to be entered ONCE (on either person) - the app draws them both ways.

villagers.name: Fadrian
villagers.notes: Son of Thadrin. Rides a horse named Gordo.

villagers.name: Stevwin
villagers.notes: Likes to hit things. Works the village smithy under Erham.

villagers.name: Snook Anook
villagers.notes: Goes by Anook. Originally from Gordin's Delve, not Stonetop.

villagers.name: Tall Pup
villagers.notes: Raised in the wild. Carries a faint memory of a dark figure and little else of her childhood. Follows Fadrian and learned from him.

villagers.name: Gerhild
villagers.notes: Wife of Berkhard. Works alongside Sithe.

villagers.name: Sithē
villagers.notes: An old, larger woman who walks with a crooked cane.

villagers.name: Alwyn
villagers.notes: A stout and jovial man who takes pleasure in providing community, rest, and mirth through food and drink.

villagers.name: Erham
villagers.notes: A man of few words. The locals find his grunts and mumbles intelligible enough.

villagers.name: Pete
villagers.notes: Jovial. Loves food and drink. An excellent cook.

map.credit: Map by Jeremy Strandberg, from the Stonetop corebook.

locations.name: The Stone
locations.notes: The Stone is well over 50 feet tall and etched in faded runes. It seems older than even the Maker-ruins (page 264) upon which the village was founded. When storms roll in, lightning strikes the Stone repeatedly. This phenomenon has made the locals somewhat impervious to sudden loud sound.

locations.name: The Public House
locations.notes: The public house is a large hall, where folks meet after sundown to drink and socialize. It offers floor space to travelers and a small stable under the same roof. The town’s horses are kept here.

locations.name: The Cistern
locations.notes: The Cistern is an underground vault, clearly an artifact of the Makers. Locals fill it with rain, snow, and water from the Stream (page 396).

locations.name: The Granary
locations.notes: The granary is a warehouse built on a Maker-ruin foundation. Foodstuffs are stored here. Everyone contributes, everyone shares.

locations.name: The Pavilion of the Gods
locations.notes: The pavilion of the gods is an open air structure with shrines to Aratis (page 22), Danu (page 64), Helior (page 224), Tor (page 452), and maybe others (page 178). As close as Stonetop gets to a temple.

locations.name: Berkhard's House
locations.notes: Where Berkhard dwells with his wife, Gerhild

locations.name: The Barracks
locations.notes: Gathering place of the local guard. Weapons and armor are housed here.

locations.name: Snook Anook & Library
locations.notes: Where Snook Anook dwells with many a book and lost arcana.

locations.name: Fadrian and Tallpup
locations.notes: The shared abode of Fadrian and Tallpup.

locations.name: Healing Houses
locations.notes: Home to Sithé and her apprentices. The town's sick or wounded are housed here temporarily.

assets: A pair of hardy draft horses
A pair of horse-drawn plows, iron
A pair of carts (plus horse harness)

improvements.name: Additional Housing
improvements.blurb: It's getting crowded! We need more room to live.
improvements.requires: Either an exceptional engineer/foreman OR building on the fields (-1 Surplus each autumn); then Pull Together 5 times, each 1 season, 1 Surplus, and a wagonload of timber (Value 2).
improvements.effect: Increase Fortunes by 1 and add new homes to the map. Henceforth, when you consume Surplus in winter, treat Population as 1 lower.

improvements.name: Aurochs Hunting
improvements.blurb: Large herds form on the Flats in spring. Stonetop has never learned to hunt them.
improvements.requires: 2 of: a Herd of Horses (and riders); cooperating with the Hillfolk; a cunning plan. Then a successful first hunt, played out in detail.
improvements.effect: Add “Aurochs hunting (meat, hide, horn)” to Resources. Henceforth, lead the spring hunt: roll +Defenses for 1d4 Surplus (with complications on 7-9 or 6-).

improvements.name: Expanded Trades
improvements.blurb: Specialization is the key to prosperity!
improvements.requires: One of: Harnessing the Stream, Raincatching, or Mill — plus at least 3 exceptional tradesfolk (chandler, glassblower, weaver, potter, smith, etc.) with good tools and supplies.
improvements.effect: Increase Prosperity by 1. If you cease to meet the requirements, decrease Prosperity by 1.

improvements.name: Greater Harvest
improvements.blurb: Beyond the Old Wall, the prairie grass chokes out any crops we try to grow.
improvements.requires: 1 of: doubling the yield of crops inside the Old Wall; or clearing/taming new fields beyond it.
improvements.effect: Increase Fortunes by 1. Henceforth, when the autumn harvest is complete, gain +1d4 Surplus.

improvements.name: Harnessing the Stream
improvements.blurb: A shallow creek flows just below the town. If only it could be harnessed!
improvements.requires: 1 of: a reservoir with a way for water to flow uphill; or a series of aqueducts from the Stream's source back to Stonetop.
improvements.effect: Add it to Resources and increase Fortunes by 1. Henceforth, when spring breaks forth and you roll 7+ with Fortunes, the steading generates 1 Surplus.

improvements.name: Herd of Horses
improvements.blurb: Imagine what we could do with a dozen fine steeds.
improvements.requires: A stable & corral site; Pull Together to build it (a month, timber); a trainer; a dozen horses; breaking them; tack (Value 2); Pull Together so villagers learn to ride (a season, 1 Surplus); a full-time handler.
improvements.effect: Increase Fortunes by 1; replace draft horses with “a herd of horses” on Assets. Herds speed Pull Together, ease Requisition, and breed/consume Surplus seasonally.

improvements.name: Heroic Reputation
improvements.blurb: Few have heard of Stonetop's heroes. Yet.
improvements.requires: Any 3 of: impressing the Hillfolk; braving a lake with proof; saving many Marshedge lives; saving many Gordin's Delve lives; saving someone from beyond Marshedge; hiring a minstrel (Value 2).
improvements.effect: Gain a move: when you first meet someone from beyond Stonetop, roll +Fortunes to know what they've heard of you (and gain advantage on 10+).

improvements.name: Inn
improvements.blurb: The public house shelters a few, but it's hardly a proper inn.
improvements.requires: In order: a building site; a competent engineer/foreman; furnishings (Value 3); Pull Together 2 times (1 season, 1 Surplus, timber each); a devoted staff.
improvements.effect: Increase Fortunes by 1; name the inn, add to Resources and map. Seasonal news via Fortunes; once per season, spend 1 Surplus at the inn to clear a debility.

improvements.name: Market
improvements.blurb: Stonetop is an afterthought for traders. We need to change that.
improvements.requires: 1 of: a good/service exclusive to Stonetop, or another reason to visit; plus a market site, a trusted arbiter, and 4 seasons without notable violence or theft.
improvements.effect: Increase Prosperity by 1 (or lose it if requirements lapse). When seasons change and Population is +1 or better, the active market generates 1 Surplus.

improvements.name: Mill
improvements.blurb: With a mill, we'd have better bread and more time for other crafts.
improvements.requires: An exceptional engineer/foreman; a consistent power source; a site to harness it; Pull Together 2 times (a season, 1 Surplus, timber & supplies each); a full-time miller.
improvements.effect: Increase Fortunes by 1; add “Mill” to Resources and the map. Autumn harvests generate +1 Surplus, and supplies stretch further when you Outfit.

improvements.name: Palisade
improvements.blurb: A wall of sharpened logs, 10' tall, to keep evil at bay.
improvements.requires: In order: ~20-25 wagonloads of timber (Value 3); a competent engineer/foreman; rope, nails, pitch (Value 2); Pull Together (a month, 1 Surplus).
improvements.effect: Increase Fortunes by 1; add “Palisade” to Fortifications and the map. Henceforth, take advantage to Deploy when you use it.

improvements.name: Raincatching
improvements.blurb: Filling the cistern takes so much work. Surely we can do better!
improvements.requires: In order: an exceptional engineer/foreman; enough slate/terracotta to roof the buildings (Value 3); Pull Together 3 times (1 season, 1 Surplus each).
improvements.effect: Increase Fortunes by 1; add “Raincatching” to Resources. Henceforth, when summer comes and you roll 7+ with Fortunes, generate 1 Surplus.

improvements.name: Standing Watch
improvements.blurb: Some full-time warriors would make us all safer, no?
improvements.requires: A veteran warrior able to command a crowd; at least 6 well-equipped, willing warriors; the village leaders agreeing to support a full-time watch.
improvements.effect: Add “standing watch” to Fortifications. Each season it consumes 1 Surplus or disbands. When you involve the watch in a move, treat Defenses as 1 higher.

improvements.name: Stone Wall
improvements.blurb: No mere palisade of wood, but a mighty rampart. We have the stone, after all.
improvements.requires: In order: an exceptional engineer/foreman; a stonecutter with an able crew; equipment & material (Value 3); Pull Together 4 times (1 season, 1 Surplus, supplies each).
improvements.effect: Add “Stone Wall” to Fortifications (erase Palisade) and the map. Advantage to Deploy when used; consumes 1 less Surplus in winter.

improvements.name: Township
improvements.blurb: Will this ever be more than a backwater village?
improvements.requires: Population +3 for 4 consecutive seasons; Additional Housing; Raincatching OR Diverting the Stream; at least 4 other improvements; a formal government.
improvements.effect: Change Size to town and Population to +0. Advantage on Muster, Pull Together, and Trade & Barter; towns generate and consume Surplus differently.

improvements.name: Weapons of War
improvements.blurb: Spears are great, but how about axes, picks, swords?
improvements.requires: Either a few dozen good weapons (Value 3); OR a smith with upgraded tools (Value 2), good iron ore (Value 2), and 4 seasons of work. Then a veteran warrior and Pull Together to train (a season, 1 Surplus).
improvements.effect: Increase Defenses by 1; add “Weapons of War” to Fortifications. Each spring spend 1 Surplus to maintain. Advanced weapons become common; swords/axes gain piercing equal to Prosperity.

improvements.name: Well-Trained Militia
improvements.blurb: Some hard drilling could make us a force to be reckoned with.
improvements.requires: A veteran warrior able to command a crowd. Then, per tactic (archery, cavalry, formations, readiness, skirmishing), Pull Together for a season of drills and 1 Surplus.
improvements.effect: Deploy with a trained tactic from a position of strength (you pick the 7-9 cost). 2+ tactics increases Defenses by 1. Each summer, spend 1 Surplus to keep training.
